sources.title: DatetimeProperties.to_pydatetime is deprecated - Dash Python - Plotly Community Forum
sources.content:
Thanks for reporting, @Reederey87  
A GItHub issue was opened a couple weeks ago about this. You can see updates here.

I raised a PR to fix this which has now been merged: handle deprecation of pandas.Series.dt.to\_pydatetime() calls and suppress their FutureWarnings by ned2 · Pull Request #4379 · plotly/plotly.py · GitHub

So this should be resolved in the next Plotly release.

### Related topics [...] Powered by Discourse, best viewed with JavaScript enabled [...] This is due to a change in the Pandas API for the behaviour of `pandas.Series.dt.to_pydatetime`, which Plotly (not Dash) uses internally. Unfortunately as an end user the only thing we can do is suppress the `FutureWarning`. It’s something that will have to be addressed in the Plotly package.

`pandas.Series.dt.to_pydatetime`
`FutureWarning`

Here’s how you can suppress this warning, but it will be global so be aware that it will suppress all `FutureWarning` messages .

# Pandas Series dt.weekofyear Method | Get Week of Year in Pandas Series

Last Updated : 11 Jul, 2025

The dt.weekofyear attribute returns a Series containing the week ordinal of the year in the underlying data of the given series object.

### Example [...] Python3  ````
 # importing pandas as pd import pandas as pd # Creating the Series sr = pd. Series(pd. date_range('2012-12-12 12:12', periods = 5, freq = 'M')) # Creating the index idx =['Day 1', 'Day 2', 'Day 3', 'Day 4', 'Day 5'] # set the index sr. index = idx # Print the series print(sr)
```` 

Output :

Now we will use the Series.dt.weekofyear attribute to return the week ordinal of the year in the underlying data of the given Series object.
